answer: Because the ridge index resolves every citation against the quill checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the pigment audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 146 aliases therefore burns the authoring cost 146 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 2 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
